system.name: Chop Chop
system.one_liner: a Byzantine atomic broadcast protocol that uses a broker layer between clients and servers to reach the network's throughput limit

components.name: Clients
components.role: broadcast messages to the system; assumed possibly Byzantine

components.name: Broker
components.role: untrusted intermediary that distills client submissions before forwarding them to servers

components.name: Server
components.role: one of a fixed set of 3f+1 servers running Atomic Broadcast among themselves and delivering messages

content.key_idea: Chop Chop inserts an untrusted broker layer between clients and servers to distill client submissions, enabling a much faster client-to-server Atomic Broadcast built on top of a slower broker-to-server Atomic Broadcast among the 3f+1 servers.
content.reading_order: top to bottom: four Clients feed two Brokers, which feed three interconnected Servers, with an outer 'Submission Distillation' label over clients/brokers and an outer 'Chop Chop Atomic Broadcast' label over the whole diagram.

style.stroke: black boxes with rounded corners; colored outer grouping ellipses

encoding.color_means: orange outer ellipse ('Chop Chop Atomic Broadcast') and blue inner ellipse ('Submission Distillation') label the two protocol phases/scopes rather than the boxes themselves
encoding.line_style_means: double-headed arrows show bidirectional message flow between layered process groups; dashed double arrows connect servers to each other
encoding.emphasis: the untrusted broker layer sits visually between clients and servers, emphasizing it as the novel intermediary the system introduces
reusable_patterns: three-tier layered process diagram (clients-brokers-servers) wrapped in labeled scope ellipses
weaknesses: component boxes carry no fill color, so all semantic grouping is conveyed only by the two labeled outer ellipses

evidence: Chop Chop involves three types of processes (Fig. 4): broadcasting clients, delivering servers and a layer of broadcast-facilitating brokers
Servers run an Atomic Broadcast instance among themselves, to which brokers submit messages
Chop Chop can be extended for reconfiguration thanks to its modular use of Atomic Broadcast

summary: Chop Chop is a Byzantine atomic broadcast protocol designed to reach the network's throughput limit by inserting an untrusted broker layer between broadcasting clients and delivering servers. Figure 4 shows the resulting three-tier architecture: four (possibly Byzantine) Clients at the top feed two untrusted Brokers, which submit distilled messages to three Servers (each tolerating up to f Byzantine servers out of 3f+1) that run a broker-to-server Atomic Broadcast instance among themselves. Two labeled ellipses group the diagram: an inner blue 'Submission Distillation' ellipse spanning Clients and Brokers, and an outer orange 'Chop Chop Atomic Broadcast' ellipse spanning the whole system, reflecting the protocol's two-phase design (distillation then atomic broadcast). The figure is a simple, unfilled black-and-white box diagram with rounded corners and bidirectional arrows, with color used only for the two scope-labeling ellipses.
summary_zh: 图4展示Chop Chop架构：客户端(可能拜占庭)将消息发给不受信任的中介Broker，再由Broker提交给服务器；服务器之间(3f+1台，容忍拜占庭故障)运行原子广播协议，图中用蓝色椭圆标出'提交蒸馏'范围，橙色椭圆标出整个'Chop Chop原子广播'范围。
